title: Taxi Drivers
description: Drive a motor vehicle to transport passengers on an unplanned basis and charge a fare, usually based on a meter.

clusters.label: Communicating with Supervisors, Peers, or Subordinates

tasks.text: Communicate with dispatchers by radio, telephone, or computer to exchange information and receive requests for passenger service.
Notify dispatchers or company mechanics of vehicle problems.
Report to taxicab services or garages to receive vehicle assignments.

clusters.label: Operating Vehicles, Mechanized Devices, or Equipment

tasks.text: Drive taxicabs or privately owned vehicles to transport passengers.
Follow relevant safety regulations and state laws governing vehicle operation, and ensure that passengers follow safety regulations.
Pick up passengers at prearranged locations, at taxi stands, or by cruising streets in high-traffic areas.

clusters.label: Communicating with People Outside the Organization

tasks.text: Determine fares based on trip distances and times, using taximeters and fee schedules, and announce fares to passengers.
Provide passengers with information or advice about the local area, points of interest, hotels, or restaurants.
Perform minor vehicle repairs, such as cleaning spark plugs, or take vehicles to mechanics for servicing.
Vacuum and clean interiors and wash and polish exteriors of automobiles.
Collect fares or vouchers from passengers, and make change or issue receipts as necessary.
Perform routine vehicle maintenance, such as regulating tire pressure and adding gasoline, oil, and water.
Provide passengers with assistance entering and exiting vehicles, and help them with any luggage.
Test vehicle equipment, such as lights, brakes, horns, or windshield wipers, to ensure proper operation.
Turn the taximeter on when passengers enter the cab, and turn it off when they reach the final destination.

skills.name: Web page creation and editing software
skills.def: Software to develop or edit web sites or individual pages. Examples: Facebook.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Operating system software
skills.def: Software to provide the operational interface to a computer and provide higher-level services and APIs. Examples: Microsoft Windows.

skills.name: Mobile location based services software
skills.def: Software to provide content or services based on a device's geographical location. Examples: Digital Dispatch, Easy Dispatch, EventHelix WebTaxi, GPC Autocab.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: Actsoft Comet Tracker, Penchant Software dispatchOffice, TranWare Enterprise Suite.
